= Glasgow Ancient Y-DNA =

This page describes the deep paternal ancestry of the principal tested Glasgow surname cluster. It deliberately stops where genetic topology stops. Y-DNA can connect tested paternal lines and estimate the age of their shared branches; it cannot identify a medieval surname bearer without a supported documentary male-line pedigree or relevant ancient DNA.

{| class="wikitable" style="background:#fff8e8; width:100%;"
! Evidence warning
|-
| Earlier versions assigned Roger de Duffeld, John of Huntingdon, John de Glasgu, Adam de Glasgu, John Glasgw of Stirling and John de Glasgow alias Smith to specific modern SNP branches. Those assignments are '''withdrawn'''. No inspected record or ancient-DNA result proves them. “Norman knight”, “Duffield Castle retainer”, “Vipont migration”, “clerical migration” and “king's armourer” are historical hypotheses, not genetic findings.
|}

== Current project topology ==

The principal working paternal path is:

:'''R-M269 → R-U106 → R-Z18 → R-Z17 → [[Space:R-S20045|R-S20045]] → [[Space:R-S14827|R-S14827]] → [[Space:R-FT4811|R-FT4811]] → [[Space:R-FT32941|R-FT32941]] → [[Space:R-FT25406|R-FT25406]]'''

The topology and date estimates should be checked against the [https://www.familytreedna.com/public/Glasgow?iframe=ysnp FamilyTreeDNA Glasgow Project public SNP results] and each branch's current Discover page because both may change as new testers and variants are added.<ref name="FTDNAProject">[https://www.familytreedna.com/public/Glasgow?iframe=ysnp FamilyTreeDNA, Glasgow Surname Project public Y-DNA SNP results], accessed 31 July 2026.</ref>

Other Glasgow or similar-surname testers may belong to different paternal lineages, including branches under [[Space:R-P312|R-P312]]. That is expected in a surname project and may reflect independent surname formation, surname adoption, an undocumented paternal event or a spelling convergence. It must not be forced into the R-FT25406 tree.

== Genetic dates ==

A branch date is an estimate calculated from observed variants and the present tester sample. It should be reported with its uncertainty, not as the birth year of a named ancestor. For R-FT25406, the project's recorded platform estimate was a most likely common ancestor around 1429 CE, displayed approximately as 1450 CE, with a much wider 95% interval of 1195–1607 CE.<ref name="FT25406Estimate">FamilyTreeDNA Discover estimate for R-FT25406, recorded 31 July 2026: most likely 1429 CE, displayed as 1450 CE, 95% interval 1195–1607 CE. The live estimate may change as testing develops.</ref>

That interval overlaps multiple documentary bearers and generations. It cannot choose between them.

== Geographic and ancient-DNA context ==

Parent branches such as R-U106, R-Z18 and R-Z17 can be compared with published ancient genomes and the distribution of tested modern men. These comparisons can supply population-level context. They do not create a personal genealogy from Bronze Age, Iron Age, Viking or Norman individuals to the Glasgow surname.

Three controls apply:

# modern testing is geographically and socially uneven;
# a parent haplogroup may have had many contemporary descendants in different places;
# an ancient sample sharing an upstream branch is not necessarily a direct ancestor.

Images and migration maps on this page should therefore be read as broad visual context only. The [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/timeline project Y-DNA timeline] is also a finding aid, not a source for a named historical relationship.

== Boundary with the medieval record ==

The documentary evidence is maintained separately:

* the [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Bearers_of_the_%27%27de_Glasgu%27%27_Name_and_the_Emergence_of_the_Glasgow_Surname%2C_c.1175%E2%80%931500 pre-1500 bearer register] establishes who is actually recorded and keeps distinct people distinct;
* [[Space:Glasgow Branches in 15th and 16th Century Scotland|Early Scottish branches]] establishes the first secure multi-generation burgh pedigree;
* [[Space:The Medieval Origins: From Normans to Glasgow|The Medieval Origins]] tests the Duffield, Norman and migration hypotheses against both the genetic and documentary limits.

The project's current conclusion is that no continuous documentary male-line pedigree joins a tested man to a named pre-1500 ''de Glasgu'' bearer. Until one does, no medieval bearer should be described as carrying R-FT4811, R-FT32941, R-FT25406 or a downstream SNP.

== Research programme ==

* Document the direct paternal ancestry of each tester to the earliest reliable male ancestor.
* Recruit independent descendants of distinct Scottish, Irish and diaspora root families.
* Compare representatives from plausible collateral surnames without presuming a historical explanation.
* Record platform topology and estimate changes with dates.
* Keep candidate medieval identifications on hypothesis pages until a testable documentary bridge is found.
* Respect tester privacy and publish conclusions at the branch level unless explicit consent supports more detail.
